title: TERRY BRUCE DIES
full_story:
Illinois Eastern Community Colleges is mourning the death of former Chief Executive Officer Terry L. Bruce, who passed away on Friday.  Mr. Bruce’s decades of leadership and public service left a lasting mark on the institution, the region, and the Illinois community college system.

Bruce served as CEO of Illinois Eastern Community Colleges from 1996 until his retirement in 2019.  Over those 23 years, he helped guide the district through a period of significant transformation while maintaining a strong commitment to students, employees, and the communities served by IECC.

In addition to his leadership at IECC, Bruce served on the Illinois Community College Board, including as Vice Chair.  Earlier in his career served in both the Illinois Senate and the US House of Representatives.  Throughout his public life, he played an important role in advancing education and public service in southern Illinois.

“Mr. Bruce’s impact on IECC and on community colleges in Illinois is difficult to fully capture,” said Dr. Ryan Gower, Chancellor of Illinois Eastern Community Colleges.  “His influence is woven into what we do every day.  He cared deeply about access to education and about strengthening the communities of District 529, and that commitment continues to shape this institution.”

“For those who knew Mr. Bruce and worked closely with him, what stood out most was how deeply he cared about people,” Gower said.  “He believed in giving second chances, and I saw him extend those opportunities time and again.  He believed in helping people move forward in their lives, and that showed up in how he led this institution and how he conducted himself personally.  He made a difference in the lives of many people.”

Bruce was preceded in death by his wife, Charlotte Bruce, who passed away in 2024.  She was closely connected to Olney Central College and its library and was a valued member of the IECC community.  Together, they shared a longstanding connection to IECC and to the communities the district serves.

The Board of Trustees, faculty, and staff of IECC extends its deepest condolences to the Bruce family and to all who knew and worked with him.

Visitation will be held from 5 to 7 pm Friday, April 24th.  Funeral services will be held at 10 am Saturday, April 25th.  Both will take place at Kistler-Patterson Funeral Home, in Olney, Illinois.

title: COUNTY BOARD MEETS
full_story:
Clay County Hospital CEO Bob Sellers announced the County Health Department’s groundbreaking will be on May 5th at 4 pm.  The board accepted a $25,000 bid for the purchase of the Burke house on the land where the new Health Department will be built.  CEO Sellers said “The name of the company buying the house will be announced when the papers are signed.”  The board approved a three percent raise for all elected county officials.

State’s Attorney Phillip Givens received approval for an ordinance for raffles and poker runs.  Givens said the ordinance allows the State’s Attorney’s office to require businesses in unincorporated county areas to complete forms for the activity and require a $25 fee for poker runs and $15 fee for raffles.  Corporate areas of the county will follow local ordinances.

Jennifer Brown presented the 911 monthly report.  In January and February 911 recorded 63 Hang up or misdials, 28 non-emergency calls, 26 Rapid SOS pings, 24 test calls, 1 text and 3 transfer calls.  Brown explained these calls are just a portion of what is received.  There are calls received on 911 that are coded differently when they come in.

Sheriff Andy Myers presented the March Sheriff’s office activity report.  There were 25 people processed through the jail during the month.  The Sheriff’s Office gave out 19 traffic citations, made 25 criminal arrests, and served 30 civil papers.  They handled 528 complaints, conducted 33 criminal and 15 accident investigations.  Sheriff Myers said they have been hammered with Freedom of Information requests which take up to four hours to complete.  He said they are working to get legislation changed.

In County Engineer Darin Koelm’s absence, the board approved a resolution to replace the bridge on County Highway 16, Ingraham Road, $125,000.

In the Executive Finance portion of the meeting, board members approved partial payment for voltage regulators for mini splits costing $1,950 to be paid out of the Capital Expenditure Account.  And, approval to purchase a recorder for the Sheriff Department, at a cost of $18,903.20, also to be paid from the Capital Expenditure Account.

Chairman Joe Goodman received approval for re-appointment of Jerry Burkett to the 911 board, for a three year term; Matthew Conklin to the Harter-Stanford Fire protection District for a three year term; Randy McNeeley to the North Clay Fire Protection District for a three year term; Timothy Hostettler to the Clay City Fire Protection District for a three year term and Andrew Bangert to the Clay City Fire Protection District for a three year term.

New business included a request for a liquor license in Larkinsburg Township.  Chairman Goodman said there would have to be a special meeting for the licensing committee.

The Claims Committee meeting was presented by Board member Janice Brooks.  Hospital paid claims were $3,497,921.89 and $240,321.82 unpaid claims; County Highway paid claims $61,871.09 and $99.65 unpaid claims; Health Department paid claims $361,995.63 and unpaid claims $58,704.22; Clay County paid claims $132,196.01; 911 paid claims $23,19574; Public Safety Tax paid claims $56,949.16; and Animal Control paid claims $10,033.42.

title: CLAY CITY SCHOOL BOARD MEETS
full_story:
The Clay City School Board met Thursday evening minus two members but still retained a quorum.

After Board President Misty Lindeman called the meeting to order there were no visitors for public comment and members quickly approved the meeting agenda and past meeting minutes.

Superintendent John Neubaum went over the Financial Report.  He noted that the district funding level stands at 86% which is about where they should be at this stage of the year.  Neubaum said at the meeting in June that they will go over the amended budget.  When asked a question about the retainer paid for legal representation, he turned to the continuing issue of FOIA (Freedom of Information Act) requests that is a problem plaguing schools across the state.  These requests have become a nuisance issue that takes an inordinate amount of time to deal with.  The state is aware of the problem but is unsure of how to tackle the problem but is looking at how to deal with it.  The board then approved the financial report unanimously.

In informational items, Supt. Neubaum said the district enrollment stands at 201.  One elementary student was added but just as quickly as that happened, the student left.  He also stated that 4 homeschooling students are taking Drivers Education classes.  On the heels of the Anhydrous Ammonia traffic accident that caused Johnsonville Grade School to be evacuated on Tuesday, Supt. Neubaum said he was contacted by Sheriff Andy Myers about conducting an evacuation drill at Clay City Schools next week.  The drill, which will include Clay City’s Volunteer Fire Department, takes place next Thursday, April 23 at 1:00pm.  Drills of this kind are important when Tuesday’s accident in Johnsonville is considered.  It was about two and half years ago when, on September 29, 2023 on U.S. Route 40 near Teutopolis a traffic accident resulted in the release of 4,000 gallons of Anhydrous Ammonia into the damp evening air that formed a toxic cloud that claimed the lives of five people in the immediate area and injured 14 others including first responders.  Changing gears, discussion moved to technology issues about the purchase of new Chromebooks for Clay City Students.  Supt. Neubaum talked about the policy of rotating the replacement of the devices every four years for specific student groups.  He said the next group to receive the new machines are Kindergarten and Fourth and Eighth Grade Students.  The discussion continued a few minutes later.  The conversation then moved on to the contract with the Clay County Sheriff’s Office for the School Resource Officer (SRO) and salary requirements for the position which is paid for by Clay City Schools.  Neubaum stated the board will take up the issue at the next meeting.  The talk then shifted back to the topic of FOIA requests with the superintendent detailing how he handles the requests that usually come in waves and require a response.

Next, Principal Brian Wattles went over student activities for the past month and included various activities including the launch and recovery of the Artemis mission a week ago, as well as students learning about the Diary of Anne Frank that also included students attending a play on that topic in Mt. Vernon.  Wattles reported that during that field trip the students stopped to eat at Culver’s restaurant and the students made a positive impression on other diners who commented on how polite and well-mannered the students were.  It was also noted that Molly Lindeman earned a scholarship for the Theater Program at Olney Central College and Jack Dye was the winner of a trip to Washington D.C. from Clay Electric Co-operative.

In new business, a number of action items were approved.  The board approved summer custodial employees including Ninetta Wilson, Deanna Brake, Kamden Bruner, Jack Dye and Jerrinn Worrell.  The board then unanimously approved the quote for new Chromebooks from Charley Inc. of Robinson for $18,690, with 30 traditional Chromebooks with a touchpad and 20 with touch screens for the youngest students.  Members then unanimously approved the quote from KCH Mechanical to replace the air conditioning equipment for the district library at a cost of $25,000.  There was a proposal to fix the existing equipment for $19,900.  But considering the superintendent’s thoughts, members opted to replace the AC unit rather than repair it.  The board also approved the replacement of one of two servers used for the school security system.  The server, from Security Alarm of Salem will handle the district’s 30 plus cameras more efficiently at a cost $27,622, with a $250 per month subscription.  The final item on the agenda was the hiring of Andrew Hillyard as the new music/band teacher for the district, on a unanimous vote.

The board then went into closed session.  When they returned to the open meeting, they approved the upholding of student discipline and then adjourned.

title: CLAY COUNTY MOBILE HOME TAXES
full_story:
The 2026 Mobile Home Privilege Tax Bills are being mailed out on Monday.  The due date for mobile home taxes will be July 1st, but you can pay the taxes at any time.  After July 1st, you will be charged an additional $25.00 per month.

If you do not receive a mobile home Privilege tax bill, and you own a mobile home, please contact the Treasurer’s office immediately at 618-665-3727 or email [email protected].  That will give the office time to investigate the matter before it is at risk of becoming delinquent.

Clay County taxpayers can pay their mobile home taxes by mail by sending their check with the payment stub to the Clay County Treasurer PO Box 88 Louisville 62858.  Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to avoid penalty.  Mobile home privilege tax bills can be paid at the Treasurer’s office in the Clay County Courthouse, they accept cash, check, cashier’s check, or money orders.  Please bring your entire bill if you want it stamped to show proof of payment.  The Clay County Treasurer’s office hours are from 8 am to 4 pm and they are open during the noon hour.  Payment can be made by placing payment in the envelope depository at the north entrance of the Clay County Courthouse.  Please include payment stub.  Tax Bills can also be paid online by credit/debit card by going to govpaynow.com PLC number a00082.

title: CLAY CITY PARENTS MEETING
full_story:
On Wednesday, May 6, at 3:15 PM, the Clay City School District will have a meeting in the district conference room.

The purpose of the meeting will be to discuss the district’s plans for providing special education services to students with disabilities who attend private schools and home schools within the district for the 2026-2027 school year.  If you are a parent of a home-schooled student who has been or may be identified with a disability and you reside within the boundaries of Clay City district you are urged to attend.

If you have further questions pertaining to this meeting, please contact John Neubaum, Clay City Superintendent or Tracy Seesengood, Special Education Coordinator, at (618) 676-1431.

title: NORTH WAYNE BOARD
full_story:
The North Wayne School Board met in regular session Wednesday night.

Board members accepted a $1000 donation to the FFA Program, courtesy of Curt Frederick, and approved an intergovernmental agreement for the Clay, Jasper, Richland, North Wayne Regional Delivery System.  They also accepted resignations from Lacey Bunting as Pre-K aide, Aaron Billington as CHS Asst. Basketball Coach, Rylee Kelly as First Grade Teacher at Johnsonville Elementary, Jasmine Moore as Special Education Teacher at Mt. Erie Elementary and Misty Ellis as CMS Asst. Volleyball Coach.

The board accepted bids submitted by Prairie Farms for milk products, firm bids from Wabash Valley Service Co. to furnish LP, Gasoline, Diesel, and from Carter Trucking for rock for FY27, and entered into an 18-month contract with Homefield Energy for Electric Supply.  Non-certified salaries and principal salaries were increased by 5.41% for FY27.

The board also hired a number of individuals for the next school year.  Amber Phillips as Johnsonville First Grade Teacher, Jim Farleigh as Johnsonville PE Aide, Meghan Obrecht as a one-on-one aide for Johnsonville, Chandler Courtright as CMS RTI aide, Lauren Grace Conard as CMS Head Volleyball Coach, Jennifer Lewis as CMS Assistant Volleyball Coach, Jayden Hatcher as CHS Assistant Basketball Coach, and Misty Ellis as CHS Assistant Volleyball Coach for the next school year.

title: ADULT EASTER EGG HUNT

title: FLORA HIGH SCHOOL CONCERT
full_story:
The Flora High School Music Department will have their Spring Concert at 2 pm on Sunday in the Harry Penry Auditorium.

The Concert will feature music from the Rock Band, Jazz Band, Concert Choir, and Concert Band all under the direction of Ethan Steber.  He says that all 4 groups have been working hard on their performances.  Steber said the concert band is excited to perform “The Great Rubber Chicken Gallop” by Randall Stanbridge, and the Jazz Band will perform Jo Jo Calypso by Jim Nadel among other songs.

The Concert will be at 2 pm on Sunday in the Harry Penry Auditorium.
